fn tokenize(src: &str) -> Result<Vec<Tok>, Error> {
    let bytes = src.as_bytes();
    let mut toks = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let b = bytes[i];
        match b {
            b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\r' => { i += 1; }
            b'(' => { toks.push(Tok::LParen(i)); i += 1; }
            b')' => { toks.push(Tok::RParen(i)); i += 1; }
            b',' => { toks.push(Tok::Comma(i)); i += 1; }
            b'+' | b'-' | b'*' | b'/' | b'%' | b'^' => {
                toks.push(Tok::Op(b as char, i)); i += 1;
            }
            b'.' if i + 1 < bytes.len() && bytes[i+1].is_ascii_digit() => {
                // number starting with '.'
                let (val, next) = parse_number(&bytes[i..]);
                toks.push(Tok::Num(val, i));
                i = next;
            }
            b if b.is_ascii_digit() => {
                let (val, next) = parse_number(&bytes[i..]);
                toks.push(Tok::Num(val, i));
                i = next;
            }
            b if b.is_ascii_alphabetic() || b == b'_' => {
                // identifier
                let start = i;
                i += 1;
                while i < bytes.len() && (bytes[i].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || bytes[i] == b'_') {
                    i += 1;
                }
                let name = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[start..i]).unwrap().to_string();
                toks.push(Tok::Ident(name, start));
            }
            _ => return Err(Error::UnexpectedChar(i)),
        }
    }
    Ok(toks)
}

**`src/lib.rs`** — `calc::eval` implemented in three stages:

- **Tokenizer** — scans `src` left to right, producing tokens with byte offsets. Numbers greedily consume digits, an optional fraction (`.5`, `3.25`), and an optional exponent that only counts if digits follow (`2e3`, `1.5E-2`); a bare `e`/incomplete exponent stays out of the number so `2e` becomes number + identifier → `UnexpectedToken(1)`. A `.` only starts a number when a digit follows; anything else that can't start a token → `UnexpectedChar(pos)`.
- **Parser** — recursive descent building an AST, matching the spec's precedence table: `+ -` (left) < `* / %` (left) < unary `+ -` (repeatable, `--2` = 2) < `^` (right-assoc, tighter than unary: `-2^2` = -4; exponent is a unary expr: `2^-1` = 0.5, `2^3^2` = 512). Identifiers followed by `(` become function calls (whitespace-insensitive), otherwise variables. Trailing tokens after a full expression → `UnexpectedToken(pos)`; running out of tokens mid-parse → `UnexpectedEnd`.
- **Evaluator** — walks the AST *after* the whole input has parsed, so syntax errors always win over eval errors, and operands are evaluated left to right so the first error found reading left to right is reported (`x/0` with unknown `x` → `UnknownVariable`, `1/0 + y` → `DivisionByZero`). `abs`/`sqrt` require exactly 1 arg, `min`/`max` at least 1 → `Arity(name, n)`; unknown names → `UnknownVariable`/`UnknownFunction`; `/` or `%` by zero → `DivisionByZero`; `%` is Rust's f64 remainder (sign of dividend).

**`tests/spec.rs`** — 14 test functions covering: all number forms, unary sign repetition, precedence/associativity, the `^` corner cases from the spec, remainder sign behavior, variables (including `abs` used as a bare variable), all four functions with nesting and whitespace, and every error variant — including the spec's exact position examples (`2 $ 3` → `UnexpectedChar(2)`, `(1))` → `UnexpectedToken(3)`, `min(1,` → `UnexpectedEnd`) and the left-to-right error-ordering rules.
